sources.intro: The research stack behind the register — live event feeds, official databases and the sources each section refreshes from, across severe storms, wildfire, floods, cyclones and drought. Reliability reflects primary-source status and update cadence.

items.name: GDACS (Global Disaster Alerts)
items.desc: Global Disaster Alert & Coordination System (UN/EC): keyless GeoJSON feed of active cyclones, floods, droughts and wildfires with green/orange/red alert levels — the backbone of the Active Events registry.

items.name: Iowa Environmental Mesonet (IEM)
items.desc: Scriptable LSR webservice and Autoplot #245: national tornado/hail/wind report counts as CSV, current through today — the refresh source behind the severe-convective bands.

items.name: SPC Storm Reports & Summary
items.desc: NWS Storm Prediction Center: daily Local Storm Reports and the current-year tornado/hail/wind summaries — the live severe-convective feed.

items.name: SPC WCM Data (report CSVs)
items.desc: The definitive tornado/hail/wind report database and running-total climatology graphics. Ingest these CSVs (2010–25) to render exact IQR/interdecile percentile envelopes.

items.name: SPC Severe Climatology
items.desc: 30-year severe-weather climatology and daily/annual summary maps — the baseline the current year is measured against.

items.name: NCEI Storm Events & SWDI
items.desc: NOAA's official Storm Events Database and Severe Weather Data Inventory — the verified record after preliminary reports are quality-controlled.

items.name: NWS API & Local Storm Reports
items.desc: api.weather.gov for alerts and observations, plus the LSR map service — machine-readable warnings and reports for automation.

items.name: NIFC Fire Statistics
items.desc: National Interagency Fire Center: year-to-date fires and acres, preparedness level, and the daily situation report — the US wildfire ground truth.

items.name: NIFC Open Data (WFIGS)
items.desc: Wildland Fire Interagency Geospatial Services: incident locations, perimeters and the day-of-year record used to build fire seasonality curves.

items.name: NASA FIRMS
items.desc: Fire Information for Resource Management System: near-real-time active-fire and thermal-anomaly detections from VIIRS/MODIS, global coverage.

items.name: CAL FIRE
items.desc: California's incident feed — acreage, containment and structure losses for the state that sets the tone for US wildfire risk.

items.name: USFA Data & Insights
items.desc: US Fire Administration statistics and datasets — the structural-fire and casualty complement to wildland data.

items.name: Copernicus EFFIS / CEMS
items.desc: European Forest Fire Information System and Emergency Management Service — burnt-area, fire-danger and flood mapping for Europe and beyond.

items.name: ESSL European Severe Weather DB
items.desc: The European Severe Weather Database (ESWD): tornado, hail, wind and heavy-rain reports across Europe — the SPC analogue for the continent.

items.name: Met Office Warnings
items.desc: UK National Severe Weather Warning Service — the authoritative UK warning feed for wind, rain, snow, heat and thunderstorms.

items.name: UK EA Flood Monitoring
items.desc: Environment Agency flood-monitoring API — river and coastal levels, flow and flood warnings across England.

items.name: IMD Mausam
items.desc: India Meteorological Department: monsoon rainfall, warnings and cyclone bulletins — the source for the South Asian flood and heat signal.

items.name: FSI Forest Fire (India)
items.desc: Forest Survey of India fire alerts — active-fire detections and alerts for the Indian subcontinent.

items.name: NHC (Atlantic / E-Pacific)
items.desc: National Hurricane Center advisories and tropical outlooks — the authority for the tropical-cyclone card.

items.name: World Weather Attribution
items.desc: How much more likely or intense a given heatwave, flood or fire-weather episode became because of anthropogenic warming.
